item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — None of the above

lookback_source.quote: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification, not how it is used, during the last 7 days or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days

lookback_notes: The N0415 item header and coding instructions state a 7-day look-back/observation period, or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. The N0415Z1 bullet itself refers only to "the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" without repeating "7-day"; the manual does not state how the 7 days are counted relative to the ARD on these pages.

coding_levels.label: None of the above
coding_levels.definition: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: None of the above (item set row)
coding_levels.definition: On the item set, row Z. None of the above has a checkbox only in Column 1, "Is taking"; there is no Column 2 "Indication noted" checkbox for this row.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415Z1 if none of the high-risk drug class medications listed in N0415 (A through K) were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications are coded in N0415 according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used; Column 1 is checked if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly (e.g., fluphenazine decanoate, haloperidol decanoate) are counted only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, only capture the medication if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics, as they are not categorized as hypnotic medications.

source.quote: Over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics, as they are not categorized as hypnotic medications.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root) are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how they are used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Step 1 of Steps for Assessment for N0415; establishes the record review supporting a determination that no listed medications were taken.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment; relevant because outside-setting administrations would preclude checking Z1.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0 pharmacological classification; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish"), though it states assessors should be able to identify the source(s).

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; the listed reference resources are optional and not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415Z to any payment or case-mix classification.
